verdict: no column may be ranked -- show counts and the number, no sort
note: Offensive units scored on 2025 play-by-play, standardised INSIDE each division and role and shown on the talent board's scale (50 average, 10 per standard deviation). Standardised because production is not level-neutral -- an FBS passer averages 1.6 standard deviations above a D3 one -- so a raw ranking would be an FBS list and would answer the opposite of the question. A 65 here means 'well above expectation FOR THIS LEVEL', never 'as good as an FBS offence'. WITHOUT TOP shows the same unit with its single largest contributor removed: a staff that holds up there is a system, and one that collapses was a player. PLAYERS lists only those still on the roster with a season left after this one; a player whose class cannot be read is left out rather than assumed available. OFFENCE ONLY -- a play-by-play names a passer, a rusher and a receiver and nobody else, so a staff whose value is its defence cannot appear here and its absence is not a verdict. NOTHING ON THIS PAGE ENTERS ANY RATING.
gate: THE COACH COLUMN IS NOT SORTABLE, and that is a result rather than an oversight. A coach's unit score persists strongly when he stays put (Spearman-Brown 0.74) and much less when he changes school (0.48 for head coaches, 0.30 for coordinators, the latter's interval spanning zero). The gap between those is the finding: most of what looks like a coach is the programme. Since this page exists to hire a person away from a programme, the school-change figure is the one that counts, and it sits below the project's 0.50 bar. It is not nothing -- the interval [+0.054, +0.541] excludes zero, so something does travel. It is too weak to rank on. The sort turns itself on if a future run clears the bar.
retro: Checked against what actually happened: of 33 head coaches who changed school in the 2025-26 cycle, 18 took at least one producer with them -- 42 players. Movers' offences were well above average either way (+0.71 z if they took players, +0.37 if not, against a league +0.12), so a productive offence does get a staff hired away. But the difference between those two groups is NOT significant at this sample (permutation p = 0.14, n = 31). This board indicates who is worth watching. It does not predict who brings players along.
